## Marsh’s Climate Adaptation Survey helps businesses prepare for the changes and challenges ahead.


Climate risk is becoming more complex, more systemic, and more immediate. Effective adaptation now goes beyond protecting physical assets, operations, and people — it also depends on the suppliers, infrastructure, and wider systems organizations rely on.


Now in its third year, Marsh Risk’s 2026 Climate Adaptation Survey captures the views of more than 120 organizations across eight regions. It looks beyond physical assets to examine the wider network of operations, people, suppliers, infrastructure, and communities they rely on — revealing where resilience is strengthening, where vulnerabilities still persist, and where the greatest opportunities for action lie.


The survey shows that, despite facing multiple climate-related hazards, many organizations are not conducting forward-looking assessments. And among those that do, many are not acting on the results. For example, 60% of respondents are grappling with multi-perils, such as flood, extreme heat and water stress, yet only just over half of the respondents are conducting an assessment.


Taken together, the survey results offer a benchmark to help organizations prioritize action and shape their climate adaptation strategies. They also highlight both encouraging progress and persistent gaps in preparedness as businesses respond to a changing physical risk landscape.
